articles.title: UBS sees limited support for a 50bp Fed hike in December despite hot October CPI
articles.description: With futures pricing slightly more than a full quarter-point hike for December, the 50bp debate is now a tail risk the market will react to on any Fed speaker headline. Treasury yields close to 5% keep the dollar supported, including against the yen ahead of the Bank of Japan’s own expected December hike, which leaves the US-Japan rate gap a key driver of USD/JPY. Higher real yields are also a headwind for gold, which has tended to trade on Fed hike expectations rather than as a safe haven this year. For equities, the combination of firmer inflation and rising long-end yields adds pressure to richly valued tech shares, which are already dealing with the Nvidia leadership shock. --- October’s inflation report makes a December Fed hike look all but certain, and UBS thinks the real risk is a faster run of quarter-point moves rather than one big step. Summary: US October CPI rose 0.4% m/m (forecast 0.3%) and core rose 0.3% (forecast 0.2%), with broad price gains The 10-year Treasury yield rose 11bp to close to 5% and the S&P 500 fell 0.4% on Tuesday Fed Governor Waller said before the data that core at 0.3% or more could warrant considering a 50bp December hike, and Dallas Fed President Logan favors at least two more 25bp hikes Fed funds futures price about 28bp of hikes for December UBS sees limited FOMC support for 50bp and keeps its base case of 25bp hikes in December and March Three-month annualized core inflation rose to about 3.75%, and tariff-sensitive and IT goods prices stayed firm A hotter than expected US inflation report has put an unusual question in front of the Federal Reserve: whether its next hike should be a double-sized one. UBS thinks the answer is still no. But the bank says October’s data strengthen the case for at least two more quarter-point increases and raise the risk that they come faster. Headline consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast. Core prices, which exclude food and energy, rose 0.3% against expectations of 0.2%. Price gains were broad, covering food, housing, recreation, medical care, electricity, airfares and delivery services. The 10-year Treasury yield jumped 11 basis points to close to 5%, and the S&P 500 fell 0.4% on Tuesday. The 50 basis point idea came from Fed Governor Christopher Waller. Before the release, he said a core reading of around 0.3% or more could justify considering a half-point move in December. Fed's Waller says a half-point rate hike in December may be needed if Core CPI comes in hot Separately, Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said she favors at least two more quarter-point hikes and suggested the Fed could move more quickly this winter. Fed's Logan: It's clear that Fed needs at least two more quarter-point rate hikes Fed funds futures now price about 28 basis points of tightening for December. That implies a full quarter-point hike and only a small chance of something larger. UBS argues that appetite on the rate-setting committee for a 50 basis point move is limited. The bank said a hike of that size could signal that policy is well below where it needs to be and make the tightening cycle look open-ended. Its base case remains quarter-point hikes in December and March. The detail behind the headline numbers explains the concern. Monthly core inflation edged down to 0.30% from 0.33%, but the three-month annualized pace rose to about 3.75%, from below 2% as recently as August. Excluding used cars, which fell 1.2%, core goods prices rose around 0.4%. Tariff-sensitive items such as toys, furniture and bedding, and appliances each rose more than 1%, and IT hardware prices climbed 0.4%. UBS noted that those categories carry larger weights in the Fed’s preferred PCE gauge than in CPI. It said goods disinflation looks a less reliable theme heading into 2027. Shelter inflation slowed to 0.30% from 0.39% but remains sticky. Energy rose a further 0.7%, although its contribution to the headline figure faded. After two disappointing reports in a row, the December debate is now about the size of the move, not whether one comes. ---- Its been a long year, final FOMC meeting coming up in 3 weeks: This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO facing ouster amid 'second affair' after Trump allows 'excuse' for first
articles.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly faces ouster amid allegations of a second affair, three days after President Donald Trump said the billionaire “probably has an excuse” for the first fling with a purported Chinese spy. Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang after he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday. Directors could meet as soon as the same day to decide his future, people familiar with the matter told the Journal. The Journal’s story followed a New York Times account that Jensen Huang, 63, had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, 48, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, who reports to him. Five people who worked at the company described the relationship to the paper. Two of those people told the Times that Jensen Huang and Powell were recorded being affectionate at a hotel in San Jose, California, during an Nvidia conference in March. The paper said it had not seen the video. “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” Jensen Huang said when a Times reporter called to ask about Powell. He then hung up. Nvidia declined to comment, and Powell did not immediately respond. “Multiple investors tell me after news of Jensen’s second affair that there’s no way he stays on as CEO,” Axios reporter Madison Mills wrote on X. She said the investors were offering opinions and did not know of any internal move to remove him. Because Powell reports to Jensen Huang, the Times account adds a workplace issue to the national security questions raised by his first affair. Nvidia’s code of conduct tells employees to “avoid situations where our actions create conflict,” including “personal relationships.” “Jensen is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption,” company spokesperson John Rizzo said Sunday, the day the board opened an investigation into reports that foreign intelligence had targeted Jensen Huang. By Wednesday, the board was preparing to do the opposite, the Journal reported, leaving Trump vouching for an executive whose own directors may push him out. “I think he’s an honorable guy, I think he probably has an excuse for it,” Trump told reporters Sunday in West Palm Beach, Florida. “There is no excuse for what I did,” Jensen Huang had written in a Nov. 8 message to employees admitting the affair, according to the Daily Beast. “I’d certainly take him,” Trump said Sunday when asked whether he would still bring Jensen Huang on his trip to Asia, which ends in China on Nov. 19. “I haven’t heard he’s done anything wrong. He dealt with somebody, but you know, so does everybody else.” The affair Jensen Huang admitted was with Alice Huang, an executive whom U.S. officials suspect of spying for China, according to the Times. The two are not related. China has denied the espionage claims, and she has not responded to requests for comment. Trump invited Jensen Huang onto Air Force One for a May trip to China after the CEO was left off the original delegation, Newsweek reported, citing the Times. Nvidia has also committed $25 million to Trump’s White House ballroom, according to documents obtained by The Washington Post. The Times has reported that Trump was briefed on intelligence about the relationship roughly a year ago. Trump said Monday that he had been hearing about it “over a period of time, but not too long ago.” “I’m sure President Xi will ask me about it,” Trump has said of upcoming talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

articles.title: FX option expiries for 11 November 10am New York cut
articles.description: There aren't any major key expiry levels that are of immediate influence today, with the full list seen below. The two larger ones for EUR/USD and USD/CAD at 1.1210 and 1.4150 respectively are the closer expiries to be wary of, although they are still some distance away with the strikes holding 40-60 pips away from the spot price. As such, the influence of the expiries are not going to all too impactful provided we see the dollar pull back more modestly in the session ahead. After the hotter-than-expected US CPI report overnight, the focus remains on the dollar side of the equation after having seen 10-year Treasury yields shoot back up to 5%. The broader risk mood was more sour yesterday too but we are seeing US futures recover some poise today in the early stages. Then again, just be reminded that it is a partial US market holiday with the bond market out of action in the day ahead. So, that will keep things a bit trickier in the sessions to follow amid thinner liquidity conditions especially during US trading later. As such, traders will be without one of the key gauges of broader market sentiment amid the absence of the US bond market later today. That could mean that any big moves might be exacerbated by thinner flows rather than any real conviction. And we as traders will not be able to say for certain which is which, before normal trading resumes tomorrow. So, be careful out there. The same goes for the dollar as well, so just be mindful on how any pick up in the broader risk mood might be reflected in the currency without the bond market backing that up yet today. In any case, the lack of any major expiries just means that traders will be left to fend for themselves in trying to work out the above conundrum in the day ahead. For more information on how to use this data, you may refer to this post here and/or refer to the Q&A below. This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.
